problem: The company wanted to re-energize the brand against a strong rival.
title: Coca-Cola replaces its flagship formula with New Coke, then brings the original back
context: Facing competition from Pepsi, Coca-Cola changed the formula of its flagship drink for the first time in 99 years.
decision_made: Replace the original formula with a new one, called New Coke.
action_taken: Launched in April 1985; the original formula returned on 11 July 1985 as Coca-Cola Classic.
observed_outcome: Consumers flooded the company with calls and letters, and the original returned after 79 days. The new-taste drink was later renamed Coke II and is no longer sold in the US.
lessons: Customers can have strong attachment to an existing product that taste tests alone do not capture.
limitations: One source gives a different return date (15 July). Sales effects over the longer term were not checked here.

claims.claim_text: Coca-Cola changed its flagship formula in April 1985 and launched New Coke.
The original formula returned on 11 July 1985, ending 79 days of New Coke alone.
